title: Build the acceptance runner and architecture gates
description:
## Outcome
Build the acceptance runner and architecture gates. The behaviour is available through the Infrastructure production path described below, with the named acceptance cases passing.

## Context
Implements Â§Â§1, 10â€“13 of DNA_CALC_REIMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md, within Bootstrap checkpoint â€” independent lanes, CI and evidence safety. Own only Infrastructure files for this task; consume prerequisite APIs rather than editing another library. Production route: cargo xtask / calcctl; call the same exported library entrypoints as the applications.

## Do
Implement cargo xtask accept --id ID --platform windows|linux|wasm|excel --require-all. Collect per-package manifests; validate test enumeration, run commands, and fail on missing/zero/skipped required cases. Add cargo-metadata dependency gates for OneCalc, skins and platform crates; deny tree-reference tokens and production-only dead seams using a reviewed call-site manifest plus integration coverage.
Add the named acceptance tests to this package's acceptance suite and register their exact names in its local acceptance manifest. Keep imported-source blob IDs and any changed semantic witnesses in the migration record. All proposed commands become real repository commands through infra-m0.3; a zero-test run is a failure.

## Port from
fresh

## Acceptance
```text
cargo test -p xtask --test acceptance infra_m0_3 -- --nocapture
cargo xtask accept --id infra-m0.3 --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id infra-m0.3 --platform linux --require-all
```
- `infra_m0_3__zero_tests_fail`: A misspelled required test name fails the runner.
- `infra_m0_3__forbidden_dependency`: Adding calc-engine to OneCalc or calc-host to CalcFml is rejected mechanically.
The acceptance runner must verify every named case actually executed and retain the machine-readable receipt. Assertions compare observable outputs, operation effects or independently instrumented calls, not a success flag assigned by the implementation itself.

## Platforms
Windows and Linux for repository/tooling execution. Artifacts produced here are consumed by wasm/browser CI; this bead does not imply running a native CLI inside wasm.

## Out of scope
Other command/function families and performance tuning. Do not add a second evaluator, a tree reference language, platform-specific code to portable libraries, or a hidden fallback. Any missing prerequisite requires an explicit dependent bead, not a local substitute.
notes:
Provisional plan ID: infra-m0.3. Native export preserves this ID; acceptance command IDs and test names use the same stable plan identity.

Handover from infra-m0.1 (2026-10-14):
1. Owner decision 2 on infra-m0.1: infra_m0_3__forbidden_dependency also proves the infra_m0_1__workspace_builds clause "prohibited OS imports fail the architecture test" (plan section 1.3, last bullet: native COM, XLL and desktop filesystem implementations do not enter portable library or browser builds). This bead's case text names only calc-engine into OneCalc and calc-host into CalcFml, so the OS-import clause needs its own observable in the architecture checks.
2. The native-only packages (calc-platform-desktop, calc-oracle-excel, xtask) carry compile_error! under cfg(target_arch = "wasm32"). No named case asserts that refusal yet: removing a compile_error! leaves every infra-m0.1 case green. Add the assertion to the architecture checks.
3. This bead adds the `cargo xtask` alias (.cargo/config.toml, which must not set build.target-dir) and updates AGENTS.md with the runner commands; the AGENTS.md Bootstrap note says so.
4. infra-m0.1 created the manifest format (AGENTS.md, Workspace section): per-package acceptance.json {"package", "beads": [{"id", "cases", "commands"}]}, cases in tests/acceptance.rs (test target `acceptance`). The runner extends the format (platforms, test target) and replaces the bootstrap form `cargo test -p <package> --test acceptance -- --exact <case> --nocapture`.
5. The default unit-test and doc-test harnesses of every library package print "running 0 tests"; the runner must never count them as executed cases.
6. The runner selects cases by --id. infra_m0_1__independent_lanes fails on any checkout that is off master or has uncommitted files, because it clones HEAD, so an unfiltered `cargo test -p xtask` fails during a later bead's pre-commit work. Never answer that with #[ignore].
7. Banned-word scan: docs/plan/ULTRACODE_WORK_PROMPT_OPUS_5_5.md states the rule and so contains both words; several imported tracker titles use the banned process noun (this bead's own title, infra-m3.20 to infra-m3.24 and others), and the case name infra_m0_5__quarantine_gate is a fixed identity. Exclude fixed identifiers; correct titles with br update, never by hand. AGENTS.md contains neither word as of infra-m0.1.
Sharpened at claim (2026-10-14):
- Runner: `cargo xtask accept --id <bead> --platform windows|linux|wasm|excel --require-all`, reached through a `cargo xtask` alias in .cargo/config.toml that sets no build.target-dir. It finds every workspace member's acceptance.json through cargo metadata, collects the cases registered for --id (an unknown --id fails), and runs only those; other beads' cases are never run, so a bead's red case fails only its own id.
- Manifest: extend the infra-m0.1 shape so each case declares the platforms it runs on (windows, linux, wasm, excel); a platform requires exactly the cases that declare it. AGENTS.md documents the final shape and replaces the bootstrap `cargo test ... -- --exact` form with the runner commands.
- Executed means: the case name is listed by the test binary's `--list` (exact match), is run with `--exact`, and libtest reports it `ok` with 1 passed. A registered name absent from --list (misspelled), a run with 0 tests, an ignored or filtered-out case, a failed case, or a missing platform each makes the run fail under --require-all. Default unit-test and doc-test harnesses that print "running 0 tests" never count.
- Not run: a case that cannot run on this host prints one line `ACCEPT-NOT-RUN: <case>: <reason>` (missing Excel, missing browser driver, missing capture) and the runner records it as not_run, red under --require-all. The marker can only downgrade a pass, never make one; no #[ignore].
- Host and platform: windows runs on a Windows host, linux on a Linux host, excel on a Windows host and records not_run when Excel is absent (the owner runs it; agents never invoke --platform excel), wasm runs the package's acceptance target for wasm32-unknown-unknown under wasm-bindgen-test-runner in both Chromium (CHROMEDRIVER) and Firefox (GECKODRIVER) and records not_run for a missing driver. The wasm route is first exercised by cfunc-m0.1; until then it is reported as not exercised, not as proven.
- Cargo started by the runner uses its own target directory (target/xtask-accept), never target/.
- Receipt: machine-readable JSON per run: bead, platform, host OS and architecture, rustc and cargo versions, HEAD, whether the tree was dirty and, if so, each dirty path with its git blob hash, the architecture-check results, and per case: package, argv, exit code, the libtest result line, outcome (passed, failed, not_run, missing, ignored), duration and log path. Written to target/accept/<bead>/<platform>/ and copied to the committed small path accept-receipts/<bead>/<platform>.json, which goes into the build commit for platforms run before it and into the close commit for platforms run after it (AGENTS.md updated to say the close commit carries .beads/issues.jsonl plus those receipts). The runner prints one line per case with outcome and exit code for close reasons to quote.
- Every `accept` run first runs the architecture checks and the word scan, whatever the --id, and records them in the receipt:
  (a) dependency rules of plan section 1.3 on resolved cargo metadata, for the host target and wasm32-unknown-unknown with all features: calc-func depends on none of calc-fml, calc-engine, calc-host; calc-fml on none of calc-engine, calc-host, calc-doc; calc-engine on none of calc-doc, calc-host, dna-onecalc, dna-calc; dna-onecalc's transitive closure contains neither calc-engine nor calc-host; no portable package's closure contains a native-only package;
  (b) prohibited OS imports (the infra_m0_1__workspace_builds clause): portable packages' non-test sources use no std::fs, std::process, std::os, std::net, `extern "system"` or #[link], and their resolved dependencies include no OS-binding crate from a reviewed deny list (windows, windows-sys, winapi and the like);
  (c) native-only packages refuse wasm32: each native-only package fails to compile for wasm32-unknown-unknown;
  (d) tree-reference tokens from a reviewed deny list seeded from plan sections 1.1, 1.3, 4.2 and 11.1 (tree reference, TreeRef, tree_ref, reference profile, ReferenceProfile, profile_id, ReferenceSystemProvider, host reference and their case variants) are absent from portable sources;
  (e) dead seams: each portable library package keeps a reviewed seams.json; every pub enum variant and pub trait in its non-test sources (parsed, not grepped) must be listed with at least one non-test call site that the check finds, and with the acceptance case that executes that caller (plan section 8.8: a manifest is necessary but insufficient);
  (f) word scan: the two banned words of docs/plan/ULTRACODE_WORK_PROMPT_OPUS_5_5.md section 0 over docs/, AGENTS.md, README.md, tracker text (titles, descriptions, notes, close reasons) and commit messages. Fixed identifiers such as infra_m0_5__quarantine_gate are excluded by name. Occurrences that existed on 2026-10-14 (about 50 across 10 docs/plan files, 11 imported tracker records, no commit message) go into a committed baseline with per-file and per-record counts that every run reports; any occurrence beyond the baseline fails. The baseline is a counted fallback owned by a follow-up bead created now.
- Each check has a negative fixture showing it rejects: infra_m0_3__forbidden_dependency covers (a), (b) and (c) (adding calc-engine to dna-onecalc or calc-host to calc-fml, an OS import in a portable package, a native-only package without its wasm32 refusal). (d), (e) and (f) are proven by unit tests of the kind this package keeps, on fixtures under tools/xtask/tests/fixtures/, never by editing the real workspace.
- New dependencies only as the Do needs them, each named in the commit message (for example syn for (e)).

Rulings after round 1 (2026-10-14, orchestrator):
- Check (e) keeps the manifest half here; the coverage half (proving the named case reaches the caller, and refusing callers inside the defining library) is owned by dc-pz3u. seams.rs cites it and every receipt counts the seam entries whose reach is unproven.
- OS-binding deny list in (b) applies to the full wasm32-unknown-unknown closure of every portable package and to the direct dependencies of portable packages on every target; transitive host-target crates such as libc or rustix are allowed.
- (d) scans non-test, non-comment Rust code of portable packages including build.rs; tests/, benches/, examples/, #[cfg(test)] code and comments are out of its scope by design and the check's text says so. include!, include_str! and include_bytes! are not followed: (b) and (d) fail when a portable package uses one, until a bead extends them to follow it.
- The runner executes each registered command of the bead (skipping and listing any that invoke `cargo xtask accept` itself) and records argv, exit code and log in the receipt; a non-zero exit fails the run.
- The direct-dependency rule that dna-calc does not depend on calc-engine (plan section 1.3: skins never depend on engine internals; section 2.1: DNA Calc reaches the engine only through CalcHost) is confirmed; flagged for the owner's M0 review.
- The seams.json files created in every portable library package are part of this bootstrap, like infra-m0.1's acceptance.json files; from now on each bead edits only its own package's seams.json and acceptance.json.

- `infra_m1_2__untrusted_workbook`: Macro and external-link activation remain disabled and a capture timeout terminates only the isolated worker.
The acceptance runner must verify every named case actually executed and retain the machine-readable receipt. Assertions compare observable outputs, operation effects or independently instrumented calls, not a success flag assigned by the implementation itself.

## Platforms
Windows with an installed, isolated Excel instance for live capture. The capture artifact and verdict replay run on Windows, Linux and wasm. Missing Excel is reported as not run, never a pass.

## Out of scope
Other command/function families and performance tuning. Do not add a second evaluator, a tree reference language, platform-specific code to portable libraries, or a hidden fallback. Any missing prerequisite requires an explicit dependent bead, not a local substitute.

title: Ship the engine-free OneCalc application controller
description:
## Outcome
Ship the engine-free OneCalc application controller. The behaviour is available through the DNA OneCalc production path described below, with the named acceptance cases passing.

## Context
Implements Â§Â§2, 4, 8 of DNA_CALC_REIMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md, within First functional milestone â€” real Excel open/recalc/edit/save/reopen. Own only DNA OneCalc files for this task; consume prerequisite APIs rather than editing another library. Production route: the OneCalc application controller with its in-memory reference provider, never CalcEngine.

## Do
Build OneCalc controller plus a minimal desktop/browser surface with formula text, typed inputs, result, diagnostics and trace. Implement a small typed workbook/sheet/name provider for references; keep CalcEngine and CalcHost absent even from transitive dependencies.
Add the named acceptance tests to this package's acceptance suite and register their exact names in its local acceptance manifest. Keep imported-source blob IDs and any changed semantic witnesses in the migration record. All proposed commands become real repository commands through infra-m0.3; a zero-test run is a failure.

## Port from
OxFml/crates/oxfml_core/src/eval/mod.rs: compiled expressions and evaluation; OxFml/crates/oxfml_core/src/binding/profile.rs: ReferenceNormalFormKey, ReferenceFingerprintPolicy. Discard ReferencePolicy, host-reference syntax and the tree profile.

## Acceptance
```text
cargo test -p dna-onecalc --test acceptance onecalc_m1_1 -- --nocapture
cargo xtask accept --id onecalc-m1.1 --platform windows --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id onecalc-m1.1 --platform linux --require-all
cargo xtask accept --id onecalc-m1.1 --platform wasm --require-all
```
- `onecalc_m1_1__reference_without_engine`: A formula reads two explicitly supplied cells and calculates correctly with only CalcFml/CalcFunc.
- `onecalc_m1_1__dependency_gate`: cargo metadata for the full OneCalc package graph contains neither calc-engine nor calc-host.
The acceptance runner must verify every named case actually executed and retain the machine-readable receipt. Assertions compare observable outputs, operation effects or independently instrumented calls, not a success flag assigned by the implementation itself.

## Platforms
Windows and Linux native tests, plus actual wasm browser execution in Chromium and Firefox. Run the same semantic fixtures on every target; platform adapters also have their native integration tests.

## Out of scope
Other command/function families and performance tuning. Do not add a second evaluator, a tree reference language, platform-specific code to portable libraries, or a hidden fallback. Any missing prerequisite requires an explicit dependent bead, not a local substitute.

- The capability to show:
  - A headless OneCalc controller in apps/dna-onecalc: a session holds typed inputs (sheet, cell, value: number, text, logical, error, blank), named sheets, and one formula text. Recomputing compiles through calc_fml::compile (a PlanCache the session owns), evaluates through calc_fml::evaluate over a small typed fixture provider (the session's ReferenceCatalog and ReferenceReader; an input the session does not hold is explicitly missing, never fabricated), and returns the result value, the diagnostics (parse diagnostics with their spans, binding refusals, EvalFault and FunctionFault, each typed and located), and a trace (the areas the evaluation asked the provider for, in order, with what it returned). No CalcEngine and no CalcHost, even transitively.
